page.layout: One block of italic Latin verse, in stanzas, with some small-capital words in roman. Running head top left, page number top right. Signature at the bottom right. No marginal notes.

p.i: Sic tanto ille magis crudior extitit, Quanto frena magis laxa cupidini Tractauit, nimia capta licentia.

At vt forte bonus montibus aduolat Pastor, qui validi pectoris[?] & manus Robur munierit follicitudine Dilecti pecoris: tum grauis irruit: Crudelemque ferum conficit, & nece Vna, seruat oues quæ reliquæ manent:
Sic tu, summe Deus, qui vigil intuens Vastantem miserè septa gregis tui Amanum, subito robore comprimens Sistis, ne solitis sæuiat artibus.
Infandúsq; cadit ter merita nece, Multos immeritos qui dederat neci: Multisq; immeritam concilians necem. Sic seruas, & oues, ô Bone, vindicas.
Pastori ergo Deo pangite carmina: Samson Christus adest. En catulus perit Vastator, fugiunt agmina Gazica.
Dauid Christus adest: millia millium Vnus dum Goliath occidit, occidunt.
Ergo continuis vocibus accinam, Quotquot sancta Dei numina diligunt, Quotquot sancta Dei robora prædicant, Quotquot facta Dei ter bona connotant.

page.notes: Verse is italic throughout; small-capital words (PASTOR, DEVS) are set in roman. "Pectoris" is the least certain reading of the damaged line 'pe_oris', copied from the scan with a [?]. Signature "D. iij." read from a small, faint mark; the numeral could be "ij" and is marked [?]. Show-through from the facing page appears on the right side and is left out.
